stem: The ages (in years) of 6 employees are: 34, 28, 45, 22, 38, 31. What is the median age?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 34 is the 4th value in the sorted list; taking the 4th value alone (instead of averaging the 3rd and 4th) is a slip in applying the even-n median rule.
Sorted: 22, 28, 31, 34, 38, 45. For n=6 (even), median = average of 3rd and 4th values = (31+34)/2 = 32.5.
33 results from rounding 32.5 up incorrectly; the exact midpoint is 32.5.
38 is the 5th value in the sorted list; this error arises from misidentifying the position for even n.

explanation: Sorted ages: 22, 28, 31, 34, 38, 45. With n = 6 (even), the median is the mean of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th values, i.e., (31 + 34)/2 = 65/2 = 32.5.

explanation_sections.punchline: For an even number of observations the median is the average of the two middle values, not just one of them.
explanation_sections.approach: Sort the data. With n=6 even, take positions 3 and 4 in the sorted list, average them: (31+34)/2 = 32.5.
explanation_sections.lesson: When n is even, median = (value at n/2 + value at n/2+1) / 2; do not round, keep the 0.5.
explanation_sections.timing: 50 s. Sort the 6 values (two passes), identify middle pair. Watch out for rounding the 0.5 away.
